More than 75% of respondents see strategic value in embedded payments, recognising their potential to streamline operations, strengthen competitive differentiation, improve customer retention and create new opportunities for growth.

Only 10.8% of businesses using embedded payments and payouts say their payment and payout experiences are fully integrated, while more than half report only basic or limited integration.

·       Speed: 56% cite the speed of funds availability.
·       Fragmented tooling: 58.5% of businesses use four or more systems across payment processing, reconciliation and reporting.
The wider findings reinforce the challenge. Only 40.5% say they have a mostly or very transparent view of their payment data. Managing payments across multiple systems can make it harder to reconcile payments, maintain visibility and make effective use of payment data.
“Businesses increasingly recognise the strategic value embedded payments can bring, but there is still a gap between that potential and the experience they have today. Visibility, speed and fragmented processes can all make payments harder to manage and limit the value businesses are able to realise.

By addressing these operational challenges and making payments easier to manage, they can deliver greater value to their customers and differentiate through the payment experience they provide,” said Rehana Mitha, Managing Director at Edenred Payment Solutions.

title: Socure and Aeropay Reduce Onboarding Friction to Only a Phone Number and Two Clicks
summary:
Socure today announced an integration with Aeropay that enables consumers to verify their identity and connect a bank account with just a phone number and two clicks. The integration combines Socure’s identity verification technology with Aeropay’s bank-linking capabilities to create a faster, more streamlined onboarding experience. For one joint customer using both solutions, the integration increased approved-customer conversion by 50%+.
Once Socure verifies a customer’s identity with merely their phone number, Aeropay’s Aerosync technology uses that verified identity to prefill and confirm the linked bank account. The customer moves straight into payment facilitation, or into cash flow underwriting based on aggregated bank transactions, without typing account details or any additional personal information.
That sequence, identity first via a phone number and bank connection derived from it, is what makes this integration a first-of-its-kind. Open banking has been used to support identity verification before; Socure and Aeropay invert it, using the verified identity to establish the bank connection, and run both inside one decisioning platform rather than two stitched-together vendors.
The gap between those systems is also where fraud lives. As AI drives down the cost of running sophisticated attacks for fraudsters, organizations on non-integrated legacy stacks are absorbing ACH returns, account takeover, first-party fraud and stolen bank credentials. These losses occur precisely because the system that verifies the person cannot see the system that moves the money. Socure and Aeropay close that gap: Aerosync handles bank verification using Socure’s identity signals, and Aeropay’s AI risk models use a decade of intelligence to screen each transaction before settlement.
“Every customer that I talk to about onboarding and ongoing authentication is struggling with the same challenge: how do they increase conversion rates while decreasing friction and simultaneously reducing fraud exposure,” said Johnny Ayers, Founder and CEO of Socure.
“Our integration with Aeropay helps our customers achieve this objective by streamlining the entire onboarding experience to one data point and two clicks, while decreasing identity and payment fraud, and increasing authentication accuracy.”
This integration advances Socure’s vision for RiskOS as the operating system for fraud, risk, identity and compliance decisions across every business unit and use case. With Aeropay in the RiskOS network, businesses can apply risk controls across the full payment lifecycle through one integration rather than three.
“Identity and payment risk can’t be treated as separate decisions,” said Dan Muller, Founder and CEO of Aeropay.
“By bringing our bank account verification and transaction risk capabilities into Socure’s RiskOS platform, businesses get a more complete understanding of both the person and the payment behind every transaction.”
